Company background 
Products & services 
Renk Group AG, based in Augsburg, is a manufacturer of advanced drive technologies, including transmissions, engines, hybrid drive systems, and vehicle suspensions.It supplies specialty transmissions for tanks, frigates, icebreakers, and industrial machinery, alongside suspension systems for military vehicles.The company has more than 3.700 employees.Renk operates 19 facilities worldwide with facilities in Germany, Switzerland, the UK, the USA, and India.
6:
Originally spun off from 
MAN SE (part of VOW:GR), Renk was acquired by Triton in 2020 and entered the public market on February 7, 2024 as a successful turnaround candidate.With an installed base of more than 180.000 units RENK also benefits from recurring revenues (~30%).~61% of European and North American tracked vehicle platforms were supplied by RENK.Since 2023, Renk has organized its business into three segments: Vehicle Mobility 
Solutions (VMS) for military and heavy-duty applications, Marine & Industry (M&I) for marine and industrial drive systems, and Slide Bearings (SB), supporting highperformance machinery across sectors.With a constant amount of ~30% of aftermarket revenues over the past 4 years, RENK has a great amount of predictable revenues.In the FY 2024, RENK achieved a highly positive performance in growth, profitability, and liquidity.Order intake increased significantly, with the VMS segment, particularly its military drive solutions, standing out as the key contributor.This resulted in consolidated revenues of EUR 1,140m (previous year: EUR 926 m), surpassing expectations.Adjusted EBIT also rose to EUR 189m (previous year: EUR 150m), supported by fixed cost degression effects and strong margins from new business.FCF more than 4X to EUR 87m, while net debt was reduced to 1.7x due to increased cash flows, reflecting a strong financial position.VMS: Vehicle Mobility Solutions (60% of revenues) 

The VMS segment is a global leader in innovation and technology for transmissions in military tracked vehicles.Beyond transmissions, its product portfolio includes engines, suspensions, electric gearboxes, and complete powerpacks tailored for military applications.Additionally, VMS is a leading provider of turnkey testing systems across various defense and industrial markets.These systems support customer 
R&D, production, and quality assurance processes in sectors such as automotive, rail, aerospace, wind energy, and military vehicles.Operating in over 70 armed forces worldwide (primarily from NATO countries) Renk holds a dominant position in its niche as the #1 supplier of vehicle transmissions and suspensions supplying parts for more than 80 types of tracked and wheeled military systems.Renk’s VMS solutions serve most tank platforms, including the 
German Leopard 2 and the LYNX.

Growth 
As a mission-critical supplier to OEMs such as Rheinmetall (RHM:GR), BAE Systems 
(BA:UK), and KNDS, RENK’s topline growth closely mirrors defense procurement trends and platform delivery cycles.With components integrated into systems across NATO members, RENK is well-positioned to benefit from the ongoing defense super cycle, driven by decades of underinvestment and multi-year replenishment needs.We expect a sales CAGR of 14.1% until 2032, including a drop in growth reflecting normalized long-term procurement programs.Moreover, the company generates ~30% of its revenues from high-margin maintenance and lifecycle support, providing long-term visibility even after vehicle delivery peaks.To support margin expansion, RENK is automating production, including robotic welding and material handling systems in its Augsburg plant.These initiatives are expected to enhance efficiency, particularly within the Vehicle Mobility segment, and support our assumption of a -4.2% decline in the COGS ratio.On the civilian side, RENK operates across a diversified portfolio, including LNG carriers, ferries, wind turbines, and heavy industry, with expected market growth of 
~3.5% CAGR through 2030 (mwb est.).While growth is significantly slower than in defense, this segment adds stability and limits sector concentration risk.Defense super cycle: 
Following the Cold War and the U.S. troop withdrawal from Iraq in 2011, global defense budgets, particularly in Western countries, saw a decline.However, since the annexation of Crimea in 2014 by Russia and amid recent major conflicts, this trend has reversed with the majority of growth yet to come.
16:
Significant military deficits now need to be rebuilt, a process demanding substantial time and financial investment.In the past years, NATO countries saw increased military spending across nearly all members.The U.S. accounted for 68% of NATO’s total military expenditure in 2023, with a CAGR of 3.1% from 2014 to 2023.This was lower than NATO’s overall growth rate of 3.3% and Germany’s 4.4% growth, despite Germany only contributes 5.3% of 
NATO’s total budget.However, these growth rates are not comparable to the growth rates in the upcoming years.Many European countries now exceed the 2% GDP defense spending target amid ongoing war in Ukraine and rising geopolitical tensions.Poland leads with 4%, while others, including Germany, are rapidly increasing budgets.Modernization efforts span all domains to strengthen defense in the Baltic and North Sea regions.Fears of a potential U.S. withdrawal from NATO have further accelerated spending (even though not assumed in our model yet).The NATO has responded with a new goal of 3.5% of GDP by 2035, signaling a long-term shift toward greater military readiness.NATO Spending (USDm)
